answer.note: The four ref files are identical and give no file-specific priority, so I chose by reading the code. I picked A (dogwhistle/study.py) and B (dogwhistle/heldout.py). Both have the two-arm verify_history(seal, ledger, reveal, public_seal, public_ledger). The incoming handoff listed A and D, but D (honest.py) and C (visibility.py) only have a single-arm _verify_history(ledger, reveal, public), so I replaced D with B. Neither A nor B meets the request as written. Their verify_history only checks ancestry with merge-base --is-ancestor. It does not reject equal commits, and it does not require the seal commit to change only its public digest file. It also compares the digest file's content at each commit, not which files the commit changed. The matching logic is in dogwhistle/listener.py: line 697 raises "seal commit changed files beyond its digest or abandonment record", and there is a seal-descends check near line 738. listener.py isn't among the candidates, so flag it to the next reviewer. Suggested 60-minute split: study.py 25 min, heldout.py 25 min, then 10 min to confirm honest.py and visibility.py are out of scope and to compare against listener.py. Nothing was run or tested. This is based on reading the code only.

def verify_history(seal: dict, ledger: dict, reveal_data: dict,
                   public_seal: Path, public_ledger: Path) -> None:
    prereg_commit = seal["prereg_commit"]
    seal_commit = ledger["seal_commit"]
    ledger_commit = reveal_data["ledger_commit"]
    for earlier, later in ((prereg_commit, seal_commit), (seal_commit, ledger_commit)):
        subprocess.run(["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", earlier, later],
                       cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, check=True)
    for relative in SOURCE_FILES:
        committed = subprocess.run(["git", "show", f"{prereg_commit}:{relative}"],
                                   cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
        if committed != (ROOT / relative).read_bytes():
            raise ValueError(f"preregistered source changed: {relative}")
    for commit, path in ((seal_commit, public_seal), (ledger_commit, public_ledger)):
        relative = str(path.relative_to(ROOT))
        committed = subprocess.run(["git", "show", f"{commit}:{relative}"],
                                   cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
        if committed != path.read_bytes():
            raise ValueError(f"published chronology anchor differs: {relative}")


def audit(run_dir: Path, reveal_path: Path) -> dict:
    registration, reveal = load(REGISTRATION), load(reveal_path)
    validate_registration(registration, reveal)
    _, seal_path, public_seal = run_paths(run_dir)
    seal, ledger = load(seal_path), load(run_dir / "ledger.json")
    if digest(seal_path.read_bytes()) != public_seal.read_text(encoding="ascii").strip():
        raise ValueError("sender seal digest mismatch")

Both have the two-arm verify_history(seal, ledger, reveal, public_seal, public_ledger). The incoming handoff listed A and D, but D (honest.py) and C (visibility.py) only have a single-arm _verify_history(ledger, reveal, public), so I replaced D with B. Neither A nor B meets the request as written. Their verify_history only checks ancestry with merge-base --is-ancestor. It does not reject equal commits, and it does not require the seal commit to change only its public digest file. It also compares the digest file's content at each commit, not which files the commit changed. The matching logic is in dogwhistle/listener.py: line 697 raises "seal commit changed files beyond its digest or abandonment record", and there is a seal-descends check near line 738. listener.py isn't among the candidates, so flag it to the next reviewer. Suggested 60-minute split: study.py 25 min, heldout.py 25 min, then 10 min to confirm honest.py and visibility.py are out of scope and to compare against listener.py. Nothing was run or tested. This is based on reading the code only.
